newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX crude extends rally to more than $1/bbl.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX crude extends rally to more than $1/bbl.

text.p: NYMEX crude futures surged more than $1.00 a barrel by late Monday, boosting refined products futures to fresh highs shortly before the close.
June crude oil futures reached a peak at $21.55 a barrel, up $1.12 on the day, before slipping slightly back, supported by renewed tensions in the Middle East.
At 1500 EDT/1900 GMT, June crude was up 98 cents at $12.48 a barrel, while June heating oil was up 2.13 cents at 56.65 cents a gallon and June gasoline was up 1.41 cents at 64.25 cents a gallon.
No supply disruptions were noted, but there was enough bullish news to lift the market through technical targets, attracting strong buying interest.
Two major crude oil suppliers, Iran and Colombia, suffered earthquakes over the weekend, though there was no news of actual damage to oil production.
Tension in the Middle East increased as a U.S. military commander pledged to protect the Strait of Hormuz amid the launch of new wargames by Iran in the Middle East Gulf.
Also, an Iraqi opposition organization said Baghdad troops were amassing in the north of the country, though Washington administration spokespeople downplayed the reports.
